content: The references provided are a comprehensive list of studies, articles, and guidelines related to lead exposure, its toxicological effects, and its management. 1. Nickel WN, Steelman TJ, Sabath ZR, Potter BK. This study investigates whether monitoring lead levels is necessary in cases of extra-articular retained missile fragments. Published in Military Medicine in 2018, it explores the potential systemic effects of lead exposure from embedded foreign bodies. 2. Barry PS. This research compares lead concentrations in various human tissues, providing critical insights into the distribution and accumulation of lead in the body. Published in British Journal of Industrial Medicine in 1975. 3. Markowitz ME, Weinberger HL. This article examines lead toxicity in children who were previously lead-poisoned, specifically focusing on immobilization-related lead release. Published in Pediatrics in 1990. 4. Mushak P. This paper discusses advancements in the toxicokinetics of human lead exposure, emphasizing the dynamics of lead absorption, distribution, and excretion. Published in Neurotoxicology in 1993. 5. Klein M, Barbé F, Pascal V, Weryha G, Leclère J. This case report highlights two instances of lead poisoning secondary to hyperthyroidism, illustrating the interplay between endocrine disorders and lead mobilization. Published in European Journal of Endocrinology in 1998. 6. Gulson B, Taylor A, Eisman J. This study evaluates bone remodeling during pregnancy and postpartum by analyzing lead levels and isotopic concentrations, shedding light on maternal and fetal lead exposure. Published in Bone in 2016. 7. Ettinger AS, Roy A, Amarasiriwardena CJ, et al. This research explores the transfer of lead from maternal blood, plasma, and breast milk to infants, emphasizing the risks of lactational lead exposure. Published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2014. 8. Rabinowitz MB, Wetherill GW, Kopple JD. This kinetic analysis of lead metabolism in healthy humans provides foundational data on lead absorption, distribution, and excretion. Published in Journal of Clinical Investigation in 1976. 9. European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). This scientific opinion addresses lead in food, evaluating its health risks and providing recommendations for safe exposure levels. Published in EFSA Journal. 10. Kosnett MJ. This chapter on lead toxicity is included in the second edition of Critical Care Toxicology, providing a detailed overview of lead poisoning management in critical care settings. Published by Elsevier in 2017. 11. Vance MV, Curry SC, Bradley JM, et al. This study documents acute lead poisoning in nursing home and psychiatric patients caused by the ingestion of lead-based ceramic glazes. Published in Archives of Internal Medicine in 1990. 12. Cullen MR, Robins JM, Eskenazi B. This article presents 31 new cases of adult inorganic lead intoxication and reviews recent advances in the literature, focusing on clinical presentation and management. Published in Medicine in 1983. 13. Janin Y, Couinaud C, Stone A, Wise L. This paper describes the lead-induced colic syndrome in cases of lead intoxication, providing clinical insights into gastrointestinal manifestations. Published in Surgical Annals in 1985. 14. te n Bruggencate CM, Lopes Cardozo E, Maaskant P, van der Waal I. This case report and literature review discuss oral mucosal pigmentation as a manifestation of lead poisoning. Published in Oral Surgery, Oral Medicine, Oral Pathology in 1975. 15. Larsen AR, Blanton RH. This case study describes appendicitis caused by the ingestion of birdshot, highlighting the gastrointestinal complications of lead exposure. Published in American Surgeon in 2000. 16. Baek SK, Bae SB, Hwang I. This article reports on perforated appendicitis caused by the ingestion of a foreign body, emphasizing the surgical implications of such cases. Published in Surgical Laparoscopy, Endoscopy & Percutaneous Techniques in 2012. 17. Greig J, Thurtle N, Cooney L, et al. This study examines the association between blood lead levels and neurological features in children affected by an acute severe lead poisoning outbreak in Zamfara State, Nigeria. Published in PLOS One in 2014. 18. Lidsky TI, Schneider JS. This review discusses the basic mechanisms and clinical correlates of lead neurotoxicity in children, providing a comprehensive understanding of its impact on the developing brain. Published in Brain in 2003. 19. Patel A, Athawale AM. This case report describes acute lead encephalopathy with optic neuropathy, highlighting the severe neurological consequences of lead poisoning. Published in Indian Pediatrics in 2005. 20. National Research Council (US) Committee on Biologic Effects of Atmospheric Pollutants. This report provides a perspective on airborne lead exposure and its biological effects. Published by the National Academy Press in 1972. 21. Perlstein MA, Attala R. This article examines the neurological sequelae of plumbism (lead poisoning) in children, emphasizing long-term outcomes. Published in Clinical Pediatrics in 1966. 22. Chisolm JJ Jr, Barltrop D. This paper outlines the recognition and management of children with increased lead absorption, providing practical guidelines for clinicians. Published in Archives of Disease in Childhood in 1979. 23. Bellinger DC. This article reviews the effects of lead exposure on children, focusing on its impact on neurodevelopment and behavior. Published in Pediatrics in 2004. 24. Needleman H. This review discusses the public health implications of lead poisoning, emphasizing the need for prevention and intervention strategies. Published in Annual Review of Medicine in 2004. 25. Needleman HL, Schell A, Bellinger D, et al. This longitudinal study examines the long-term effects of low-dose lead exposure in childhood, with an 11-year follow-up. Published in New England Journal of Medicine in 1990. 26. Tong S. This article explores the persistence and dynamic patterns of lead exposure's effects on cognitive development in children. Published in Journal of Paediatrics and Child Health in 1998. 27. Reuben A, Caspi A, Belsky DW, et al. This study investigates the association between childhood blood lead levels and cognitive function, socioeconomic status, and IQ changes into adulthood. Published in JAMA in 2017. 28. Reuben A, Elliott ML, Abraham WC, et al. This research links childhood lead exposure to structural brain integrity in midlife, as assessed by MRI. Published in JAMA in 2020. 29. Lanphear BP, Hornung R, Khoury J, et al. This pooled analysis examines the relationship between low-level environmental lead exposure and children's intellectual function. Published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2005. 30. Crump KS, Van Landingham C, Bowers TS, et al. Published in Critical Reviews in Toxicology in 2013. 31. Shobha N, Taly AB, Sinha S, et al. Published in British Medical Journal in 2018. 36. Lanphear BP, Rauch S, Auinger P, et al. This population-based cohort study examines the relationship between low-level lead exposure and mortality in US adults. Published in Lancet Public Health in 2018. 37. Lewington S, Clarke R, Qizilbash N, et al. Published in Lancet in 2002. 38. Cartón JA, Llorente R, Arribas JM, et al. This comparative therapeutic study evaluates the efficacy of low-dose d-penicillamine and disodium calcium EDTA in acute lead poisoning. Published in Medicina Clínica in 1985. 39. Loghman-Adham M. This article reviews the renal effects of environmental and occupational lead exposure, emphasizing the mechanisms of nephrotoxicity. Published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 1997. 40. Cullen MR, Kayne RD, Robins JM. This study explores endocrine and reproductive dysfunction in men associated with occupational inorganic lead intoxication. Published in Archives of Environmental Health in 1984. 41. Bastrup-Madsen P. This article discusses the use of dimercaprol in the treatment of acute lead poisoning, providing historical insights into chelation therapy. Published in Lancet in 1950. 42. This study examines the clinical findings and diagnostic tests for acute-subacute lead poisoning. Published in Archives of Internal Medicine in 1987. 44. Kosnett MJ, Wedeen RP, Rothenberg SJ, et al. This article provides recommendations for the medical management of adult lead exposure, emphasizing prevention and treatment strategies. Published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2007. 45. Davoli CT, Serwint JR, Chisolm JJ Jr. This study focuses on asymptomatic children with venous lead levels exceeding 100 µg/dL, highlighting the importance of early detection and intervention. Published in Pediatrics in 1996. 46. Toxicological profile for lead. This comprehensive report by the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry provides an in-depth analysis of lead's toxicological effects. 47. Measurement procedures for determining lead concentrations in blood and urine. This guideline outlines standardized methods for assessing lead exposure in clinical and laboratory settings. 48. Parsons P, Reilly A, Esernio-Jenssen D. This study evaluates the accuracy of capillary blood lead fingerstick tests for screening children exposed to lead. Published in Clinical Chemistry in 1997. 49. Promoting health: Guide to national implementation of the Shanghai Declaration. This document provides a framework for implementing public health strategies to reduce lead exposure. 50. Lead in: Chemical safety and health. This resource discusses the health impacts of lead exposure and strategies for chemical safety. 51. Détermination de nouveaux objectifs de gestion des expositions au plomb. This French-language report outlines new objectives for managing lead exposure. 52. Wilhelm M, Beinzow B, Angerer J, et al. This study reassesses critical lead effects, leading to the suspension of human biomonitoring values for lead in blood. Published in International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health in 2010. 53. Schulz C, Angerer J, Ewers U, et al. This article discusses the role of the German Human Biomonitoring Commission in evaluating lead exposure. Published in International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health in 2007. 54. Advisory Committee on Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention. This report emphasizes the harms of low-level lead exposure in children and calls for renewed efforts in primary prevention. 55. Lead, elevated blood lead levels. This case definition outlines criteria for diagnosing elevated blood lead levels as part of the National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System. 56. Rees N, Fuller R. This report highlights the detrimental effects of lead pollution on children's health and future potential, emphasizing the need for global action. 57. Hwang YH, Hsiao CK, Lin PW. This study examines global trends in blood lead levels among preschool children, stratified by Human Development Index categories. Published in Science of the Total Environment in 2019. 58. Lead report 2019: Broken Hill children less than 5 years old. This report provides data on lead exposure in young children from Broken Hill, Australia. 59. Whitehead LS, Buchanan SD. This article discusses childhood lead poisoning as an ongoing environmental justice issue. Published in Journal of Public Health Management and Practice in 2019. 60. Calain P. This commentary addresses ethical dilemmas in population-level treatment of lead poisoning, using the Zamfara State crisis as a case study. Published in Public Health Ethics in 2014. 61. American Academy of Clinical Toxicology, European Association of Poisons Centres and Clinical Toxicologists. This position paper evaluates the use of single-dose activated charcoal for gastrointestinal decontamination. Published in Clinical Toxicology in 2005. 62. Höjer J, Troutman WG, Hoppe K, et al. This updated position paper discusses the use of ipecac syrup for gastrointestinal decontamination. Published in Clinical Toxicology in 2013. 63. Benson BE, Hoppe K, Troutman WG, et al. This position paper update evaluates the role of gastric lavage in gastrointestinal decontamination. Published in Clinical Toxicology in 2013. 64. American Academy of Clinical Toxicology, European Association of Poisons Centres and Clinical Toxicologists. This position paper discusses the use of cathartics in managing lead poisoning. Published in Clinical Toxicology in 2004. 65. Thanacoody R, Caravati EM, Troutman WG, et al. This position paper update reviews the use of whole bowel irrigation for gastrointestinal decontamination in overdose patients. Published in Clinical Toxicology in 2015. 66. Daubert GP. This case report describes lead poisoning in a young boy, emphasizing the importance of early diagnosis and management. Published in Consult Pediatricians in 2006. 67. Communicating radiation risks in pediatric imaging. This document provides information to support healthcare discussions about the benefits and risks of radiation exposure in children. 68. McKinney PE, McKinney P. This case study describes acute elevation of blood lead levels following the ingestion of large quantities of lead shot. Published in Clinical Toxicology in 2000. 69. Cooney DO. This chapter discusses the effects of activated charcoal on various inorganic substances, including lead. Published in Activated Charcoal in Medical Applications in 1995. 70. Schwarz KA, Alsop JA. This case report describes the successful outpatient treatment of pediatric lead ingestion using whole bowel irrigation. Published in Clinical Toxicology in 2008. 71.
